_comment: OWASP GenAI Security Project reference ids. Titles and ids are facts; every summary is this project's own wording, because the OWASP documents are CC BY-SA 4.0 and this repository's data is CC BY 4.0. Regenerate MAPPINGS indexes with scripts/sync_mappings.py after editing.

agentic_2026.cross_map_note: related_llm_2025 is Appendix A as published; related_llm_2026 is the same list translated through llm_2025_to_2026. threat_ids are the Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations T-codes.

ASI01.title: Agent Goal Hijack
ASI01.summary: Content the agent reads - a document, a web page, a tool result, a message - redirects what the agent is trying to accomplish, so it pursues an attacker's objective with the user's authority.

ASI02.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
ASI02.summary: The agent uses tools it was legitimately given in an unsafe or unintended way - chaining them, over-calling them or passing them attacker-shaped arguments - without any tool being vulnerable itself.

ASI03.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
ASI03.summary: Credentials, tokens and delegated permissions held by or passed through an agent are reused, inherited or escalated beyond what the task needed.

ASI04.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
ASI04.summary: A third-party component the agent loads at runtime - an MCP server, plugin, tool definition, model, prompt template or agent card - is malicious or compromised.

ASI05.title: Unexpected Code Execution
ASI05.summary: Agent-generated or agent-fetched code, commands or deserialised content execute on a host where nobody intended arbitrary execution.

ASI06.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
ASI06.summary: Persistent memory, retrieved context or shared state is seeded with content that changes the agent's later behaviour, surviving the session that planted it.

ASI07.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.summary: Messages between agents are spoofed, intercepted, replayed or trusted without authentication, so one agent can be steered through another.

ASI08.title: Cascading Failures
ASI08.summary: One faulty or compromised step propagates through automated agent chains and amplifies into a wider failure before a human can intervene.

ASI09.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
ASI09.summary: The agent's apparent authority or fluency is used to get a human to approve, run or believe something they would otherwise reject.

ASI10.title: Rogue Agents
ASI10.summary: An agent drifts from, conceals or acts against its intended behaviour - through compromise or misalignment - while still appearing to operate normally.
